title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
summary: Looping in transformer models reuses weights by repeatedly applying the same transformer, or parts of it, making the model deeper without increasing its parameter count. Whether looping is useful depends on which constraint dominates: model size, training compute, or autoregressive inference efficiency. We study these trade-offs jointly in dense decoder-only transformers trained from scratch, varying which parts of the model are looped, how many loops are applied, and how information is passed between loops. Our experiments span models with up to 1B parameters, trained on up to 155B tokens with up to $1.07\times10^{21}$ FLOPs and 32 loops. We find that looping the full transformer generally gives the strongest quality at a fixed parameter budget, whereas looping a middle block of layers gives a better return when training FLOPs are constrained. Adding loops is not uniformly beneficial: gains eventually saturate, reverse, or become unstable. This motivates asking whether forcing every loop to use the same weights limits the benefit of deeper looping. We address this by adding small loop-specific low-rank adapters that improve quality, with larger gains as more loops are added. Looped transformers also suffer a decoding slowdown proportional to the number of loops. Parallel Loop Transformers address this by passing hidden states between loops across adjacent token positions, allowing loop stages to run concurrently. However, in our experiments the original formulation does not consistently retain the quality gains of ordinary looping. We find that preserving the current-token embedding and separately normalizing it and the previous-token hidden state before combining them recovers strong performance across model scales and training budgets. Together, these results show that effective looping requires matching the design to the resource constraint and inference setting.

title: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes
summary: Objectives: To evaluate the accuracy and calibration of Decision and System One models on rheumatology examination questions and diagnostic vignettes. Methods: Two benchmarks were analysed: 172 rheumatology questions from Spanish specialty-training examinations (expanded RheumaMIR dataset) in Spanish and English, and 70 English diagnostic vignettes from RheumBench with 5-18 candidate diagnoses, 52 of which included the reference diagnosis. Four System One models (Jev 1.13, Clef, Microsoft-Decision-1, Laya) and GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI Decisions API) were compared with GPT-6 Sol and two local generative models. The primary outcome was accuracy; secondary outcomes included calibration, discrimination, accuracy of answers with probability >=0.90 and language differences. Results: In RheumaMIR, Jev's accuracy was 93.0% in Spanish and 91.9% in English, below GPT-6 Sol (99.4%; Holm-adjusted P<=0.005); GPT-6 Luna reached 97.7%, Clef 91.9-93.0% and Microsoft-Decision-1 86.0-87.8%, without detectable language differences. Jev's answers with probability >=0.90 (76-77% of answers) were 98.5% correct. In RheumBench, accuracy was lower: GPT-6 Sol 76.9%, GPT-6 Luna 63.5%, Clef 59.6%, Jev 50.0% and Microsoft-Decision-1 40.4% (each System One model below GPT-6 Sol, Holm-adjusted P<=0.045; chance 9.6%). Jev became overconfident (mean probability 0.659; over/underconfidence index +0.159), and its answers with probability >=0.90 (25% of cases) were 84.6% correct, against 95.5% for GPT-6 Luna (42%). Laya performed near chance in both benchmarks. Conclusion: The best-performing System One models were highly accurate on examination questions but less accurate on diagnostic vignettes, remaining below GPT-6 Sol. Jev's high-confidence predictions were less reliable on vignettes, highlighting the need for task-specific evaluation and calibration.

title: Hammering with Vampire in Lean
summary: We present Vampire-Hammer, a hammer for the Lean interactive theorem prover that discharges goals using the Vampire automated theorem prover and reconstructs proofs checked by the Lean kernel. Vampire-Hammer uses the Lean-auto framework to process goals and premises before dispatching them to Vampire for proof search. Doing so, we rely on standard TPTP problem formats and annotated TSTP proofs that support proof reconstruction. With a 10-second budget on 196,083 eligible Mathlib theorems, Vampire-Hammer solves 21,158 problems not solved by other evaluated tools within the same budget.

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
summary: A multi-agent framework using large language models for stock trading simulates real-world trading firms, improving performance metrics like cumulative returns and Sharpe ratio.

title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
summary: Harness² improves agent execution harnesses through recursive task-level refinement and continual harness-level learning, boosting performance across benchmarks without ground-truth verifiers.

title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
summary: TokenEconomizer reduces recurring token costs of coding agents across sequential real-world tasks by pruning irrelevant tools, injecting micro-skills, and interrupting failure loops.

title: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction
summary: Edge0 enables efficient mixture-of-experts inference on consumer hardware by predicting expert routing ahead of time and using recovery adapters to maintain quality with minimal active memory.

title: Unlimited OCR Works
summary: Unlimited OCR introduces Reference Sliding Window Attention to eliminate growing memory consumption during long-sequence OCR tasks, enabling efficient transcription of multiple pages in a single forward pass.

title: Very Large-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation in AgentScope
summary: Enhancements to the AgentScope platform improve scalability, efficiency, and ease of use for large-scale multi-agent simulations through distributed mechanisms, flexible environments, and user-friendly tools.

title: AgentScope 1.0: A Developer-Centric Framework for Building Agentic Applications
summary: AgentScope enhances agentic applications by providing flexible tool-based interactions, unified interfaces, and advanced infrastructure based on the ReAct paradigm, supporting efficient and safe development and deployment.

title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
summary: Investor's Last Exam evaluates financial agents on end-to-end equity research using frozen evidence, expert criteria, and dependency graphs, revealing that top models excel at research but fail at forecasting and investment judgments.

title: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
summary: Kronos, a specialized pre-training framework for financial K-line data, outperforms existing models in forecasting and synthetic data generation through a unique tokenizer and autoregressive pre-training on a large dataset.

title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
summary: MOSS-Image is an open diffusion transformer that combines high-fidelity synthesis with intent-aware prompt enhancement to generate text-rich, layout-coherent images, achieving state-of-the-art open-weight results on long-form text and layout benchmarks.

title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
summary: Intrinsic Distribution Matching improves few-step text-to-image generation by adding explicit moment constraints to distribution matching distillation, achieving state-of-the-art long-text rendering with minimal network evaluations.

title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
summary: Hy-Nomas is a video world model that uses causal attention and structured conditioning to generate interactive, multi-turn video segments with text and camera control.

title: OpenDevin: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
summary: OpenDevin is a platform for developing AI agents that interact with the world by writing code, using command lines, and browsing the web, with support for multiple agents and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
summary: PagedAttention algorithm and vLLM system enhance the throughput of large language models by efficiently managing memory and reducing waste in the key-value cache.

title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
summary: Assistants from 2011 answered and waited, and agents from 2023 did a task and stopped. In September 2026 Meta's Muse showed an agent for one person, with accounts, devices, memory and a conversation that lasts, closed, in a vendor's cloud, in one country. Such an agent is expected to act on a person's accounts and devices, remember them across weeks, speak first when it is worth it, and answer for what it did. It is a kind of software, not a model, and until now had no open counterpart. This report defines the personal agent in five questions and three horizons. It reads how Muse is built from Meta's public record and a copy of its production prompt, each statement marked by its source. It then presents nanoMuse, the open-source counterpart under the GPL-3.0, one agent on every device a person owns, with hands on the phone's screen and the computer's. They share one conversation over a relay anyone can run; every action goes through a Sentinel, memory is files the person can read, and the model is their choice. Its size and cost are given as estimates. What is open, memory with provenance, an evaluation suite for the hands and an open model for them, is set out as a roadmap.

title: MinerU2.5: A Decoupled Vision-Language Model for Efficient High-Resolution Document Parsing
summary: MinerU2.5, a 1.2B-parameter document parsing vision-language model, achieves state-of-the-art recognition accuracy with computational efficiency through a coarse-to-fine parsing strategy.

title: SmolDocling: An ultra-compact vision-language model for end-to-end multi-modal document conversion
summary: SmolDocling is a compact vision-language model that performs end-to-end document conversion with robust performance across various document types using 256M parameters and a new markup format.

title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6: Expanding the Frontier of Document Parsing with Under-Optimized Region Refinement and Progressive Post-Training
summary: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 enhances document parsing performance through targeted data optimization and progressive post-training techniques, achieving state-of-the-art results on OmniDocBench v1.6.

title: Prism: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Native 2K Joint Video-Audio Generation Model Training
summary: Prism accelerates native joint video-audio generation at 2K by using dynamic sparse attention guided by local visual variance and audio-visual cross-attention to preserve semantic coherence and cross-modal interactions.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
summary: Mem0, a memory-centric architecture with graph-based memory, enhances long-term conversational coherence in LLMs by efficiently extracting, consolidating, and retrieving information, outperforming existing memory systems in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
summary: Frontier large language models exhibit Internal Safety Collapse, where they generate harmful content under specific task conditions, revealing inherent vulnerabilities despite alignment efforts.

title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
summary: Next-Concept Modeling uses hierarchical discrete codes and parallel level-wise generation to accelerate diffusion language models while improving quality and reasoning performance.

title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
summary: DynaFlow enables adaptive multi-agent collaboration by letting a main agent synthesize executable workflows that coordinate sub-agents through structured execution and verification.

title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
summary: WeVisOne-VL unifies object-level and pixel-level visual perception via structured token prediction, supporting detection, localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting with a lightweight pixel decoder and multi-stage training.

title: ARIS: Autonomous Research via Adversarial Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: ARIS is an open-source research harness that uses cross-model adversarial collaboration to ensure reliable long-term research outcomes through coordinated execution, orchestration, and assurance layers.

title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
summary: AutoTavern demonstrates that self-improving LLM research agents can autonomously build a faithful game simulator and train a reinforcement learning agent that surpasses top human players in Hearthstone Battlegrounds.

title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
summary: StreamEval benchmarks interactive streaming video generation across five tasks, revealing that reliable request execution and sustained state consistency remain major challenges despite high visual quality.

title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
summary: A pipeline using sparse autoencoders extracts interpretable linguistic features from neural detectors, yielding more accurate and explainable AI-generated text classification.

title: YuE2: Unifying Symbolic and Audio Music Generation at Frontier Quality
summary: YuE2 unifies symbolic and audio music generation via symbolic planning, producing readable scores and full-song audio with state-of-the-art quality and agentic editing capabilities.

title: Geometric Context Transformer for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
summary: LingBot-Map is a feed-forward 3D foundation model that reconstructs scenes from video streams using a geometric context transformer architecture with specialized attention mechanisms for coordinate grounding, dense geometric cues, and long-range drift correction, achieving stable real-time performance at 20 FPS.

metadata.readme_excerpt: Paritok A non-destructive compression gateway for coding agents — cut your input-token bill without changing your agent. Paritok sits between your agent and the LLM as a drop-in proxy. On every request it strips the tool-schema bloat, compresses tool results and file reads, and summarizes stale history — then forwards upstream, billed on the compressed tokens. Nothing is ever permanently discarded: the agent pulls back any exact original on demand. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenHands , and any agent that honors BASE_URL — you don't change a line of your agent . Powered by the first open-source 4B compression model trained specifically for coding agents (45K real agent trajectories). Cut input token bills from ~25% on turn one to past 85% in long, context-saturated sessions , and fit ~3× more turns in the same context window. Strip grammar. Keep facts. Save tokens. ```diff - "In order to optimize the database query performance, we should consider implementing an index on the frequently accessed columns..." (70 tokens) + "Need fast queries. Check which columns used most. Add index to those columns..." (50 tokens) = 29% reduction ``` --- ## How It Works ![How Caveman Compression Works](images/info.png) LLMs excel at filling linguistic gaps. They predict missing grammar, connectives, and structure. **Key insight:** We remove only what LLMs can reliably reconstruct. **What we remove (predictable):** - Grammar: "a", "the", "is", "are" - Connectives: "therefore", "however", "because" - Passive constructions: "is calculated by" - Filler words: "very", "quite", "essentially" **What we keep (unpredictable):** - Facts: numbers, names, dates - Technical terms: "O(log n)", "binary search" - Constraints: "medium-large", "frequently accessed" - Specifics: "Stockholm", "99.9% uptime" ``` Compressed: "Company medium-large. Instead of extending token-based context windows, Glyph renders long textual sequences into images and processes them using vision–language models (VLMs). This design transforms the challenge of long-context modeling into a multimodal problem, substantially reducing computational and memory costs while preserving semantic information. (Upper) Comparison of two paradigms for long-context tasks: conventional approaches directly feeding plain text into LLMs, and the proposed VLM-based paradigm, Glyph, which renders text as compact images to achieve substantial input-token compression. summary: 中文LLaMA-2 & Alpaca-2大模型二期项目 + 64K超长上下文模型 (Chinese LLaMA-2 & Alpaca-2 LLMs with 64K long context models) | **🇨🇳中文** | **🌐English** | **📖文档/Docs** | **❓提问/Issues** | **💬讨论/Discussions** | **⚔️竞技场/Arena** 本项目基于Meta发布的可商用大模型Llama-2开发,是中文LLaMA&Alpaca大模型的第二期项目,开源了**中文LLaMA-2基座模型和Alpaca-2指令精调大模型**。这些模型**在原版Llama-2的基础上扩充并优化了中文词表**,使用了大规模中文数据进行增量预训练,进一步提升了中文基础语义和指令理解能力,相比一代相关模型获得了显著性能提升。相关模型**支持FlashAttention-2训练**。标准版模型支持4K上下文长度,**长上下文版模型支持16K、64k上下文长度**。**RLHF系列模型**为标准版模型基础上进行人类偏好对齐精调,相比标准版模型在**正确价值观体现**方面获得了显著性能提升。 - 🚀 针对Llama-2模型扩充了**新版中文词表**,开源了中文LLaMA-2和Alpaca-2大模型 - 🚀 开源了预训练脚本、指令精调脚本,用户可根据需要进一步训练模型 - 🚀 使用个人电脑的CPU/GPU快速在本地进行大模型量化和部署体验 - 🚀 支持🤗transformers, llama.cpp, text-generation-webui, LangChain, privateGPT, vLLM等LLaMA生态 - 基座模型(4K上下文):Chinese-LLaMA-2 (1.3B, 7B, 13B) - 聊天模型(4K上下文):Chinese-Alpaca-2 (1.3B, 7B, 13B) - Chinese-LLaMA-2-16K (7B, 13B) 、Chinese-Alpaca-2-16K (7B, 13B) - Chinese-LLaMA-2-64K (7B)、Chinese-Alpaca-2-64K (7B) - 偏好对齐模型:Chinese-Alpaca-2-RLHF (1.3B, 7B) 中文LLaMA&Alpaca大模型 | 多模态 | Stars: 7099 | Language: Python

metadata.readme_excerpt: # RedKnot + DeepInfer The DeepInfer-based development track of **RedKnot**, an open-source project for efficient long-context LLM serving. [Website](https://rednote-machine-learning.github.io/RedKnot/) · [RedKnot paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06256) · [Upstream DeepInfer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer) · [Apache-2.0 license](LICENSE) **Status:** This branch starts from the complete [DeepInfer baseline at `5537415`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/commit/553741557a57df44a46fb3ab72b6aafeaf945337), including its pinned submodules. The [RedKnot benchmark harness](benchmarks/redknot/README.md) now migrates the SGLang release datasets and suites to frozen target-tokenizer inputs, with a native DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash baseline runner. RedKnot's optimized native execution and additional model implementations remain pending. The DeepInfer sections below describe the upstream baseline. ## Framework branches | Branch | Purpose | | --- | --- | | **[RedKnot+DeepInfer](https://github.com/rednote-machine-learning/RedKnot/tree/RedKnot%2BDeepInfer)** | **Default branch** · DeepInfer baseline for RedKnot development | | [RedKnot-SGLang](https://github.com/rednote-machine-learning/RedKnot/tree/RedKnot-SGLang) | SGLang-based RedKnot implementation; formerly `main` | | [RedKnot-vLLM](https://github.com/rednote-machine-learning/RedKnot/tree/RedKnot-vLLM) | vLLM adaptation track | RedKnot belongs to its contributors. metadata.readme_excerpt: Long-term memory for AI assistants — fast, private, and yours. # AutoMem [AutoMem](https://automem.ai) gives your AI a memory that survives the chat. Save the decisions, preferences, notes, and context that matter. The next time you open Claude, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, or another connected assistant, it can bring back the right details instead of making you repeat yourself. Ask, "Why did we choose PostgreSQL?" and AutoMem can return the decision, the alternatives you considered, the principle behind it, and the work that followed — not just a pile of similarly worded snippets. ## Why AutoMem feels different **No LLM call in the middle of recall.** AutoMem looks up memories directly through its graph and vector index. That keeps normal retrieval fast and avoids an extra generative-LLM charge every time your assistant needs context. It still uses embeddings — from Voyage, OpenAI, or a local provider — and optional enrichment can add more structure over time. **More than vector search.** A vector match finds something similar; AutoMem also records typed relationships between memories. It can follow the connections between a decision, its rationale, and its consequences, so your assistant has a better chance of returning the *why*, not only the words it recognizes. **One memory across your tools.** Use the local MCP bridge with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and more. For cloud agents, Remote MCP connects the same service to ChatGPT Developer Mode, Claude.ai, and ElevenLabs over HTTPS. Your memory is not locked to one chat app. **Own the data and the setup.** Run AutoMem locally with Docker, on your own infrastructure, or as a small Railway service group. It exposes both MCP and a REST API, so it fits into the tools and workflows you already use. ## Pr

While various model-based methods have improved sample efficiency by learning interactive world models, these agents tend to be "short-sighted", as they are typically trained on short snippets of imagined experiences. We argue that the primary challenge in open-world decision-making is improving the exploration efficiency across a vast state space, especially for tasks that demand consideration of long-horizon payoffs. In this paper, we present LS-Imgine, which extends the imagination horizon within a limited number of state transition steps, enabling the agent to explore behaviors that potentially lead to promising long-term feedback. The foundation of our approach is to build a long short-term world model . To achieve this, we simulate goal-conditioned jumpy state transitions and compute corresponding affordance maps by zooming in on specific areas within single images. This facilitates the integration of direct long-term values into behavior learning. Frontier agentic models have already begun to exhibit this capability in the digital domain, where they reason over goals, invoke tools, inspect execution results, and complete long-horizon tasks through feedback. What they still lack is a reliable way to extend that loop into the physical world. OpenETA explores this transition from Digital Agent to Physical Agent as a new paradigm. Instead of reducing embodied intelligence to a single observation-to-action model, it places the Agent inside the world's causal chain so that perception, action, verification, and learning become one continuous process. Intelligence moves beyond processing digital information and begins to understand and change reality. Du](https://simonshaoleidu.com/), [Antonio Torralba](https://web.mit.edu/torralba/www/), [Phillip Isola](https://web.mit.edu/phillipi/), [Amy Zhang](https://amyzhang.github.io/), [Yuandong Tian](https://yuandong-tian.com/)** We provide a PyTorch implementation of [Denoised MDPs: Learning World Models Better Than The World Itself](https://ssnl.github.io/denoised_mdp), published in ICML 2022. + [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15477) + [Project Page](https://ssnl.github.io/denoised_mdp) (We also provide a PyTorch implementation of [Dreamer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.01603) that is carefully written and verified to reproduce results. See [here](#reproducing-dreamer) for usages.) The raw real world is noisy. How can reinforcement learning agent successfully learn with such raw data, where signals can be strongly entangled with noises? Denoised MDP characterizes information into four distinct types, based on controllability and relation with rewards, and proposes to extract a state representation space containing only information both **controllable** and **reward-relevant**. Under this view, several prior works can be seen as insufficiently removing noisy information. To properly extract *only* the useful signal, Denoised MDP considers novel factorized MDP transition structures, where **signal** representation and **noise** representation are separated into distinct latent spaces. The state abstraction (i.e., representation learning) problem is turned into a regularized model fitting problem: fitting the factorized forward model to collected trajectories, while requiring the **signal** latents to be minimally informative of the raw observations. metadata.readme_excerpt: # C3-OWD: A Curriculum Cross-modal Contrastive Learning Framework for Open-World Detection --- # 👋 Introduction Object detection has advanced significantly in the closed-set setting, but real-world deployment remains limited by two challenges: poor generalization to unseen categories and insufficient robustness under adverse conditions. Prior research has explored these issues separately: visible-infrared detection improves robustness but lacks generalization, while open-world detection leverages vision-language alignment strategy for category diversity but struggles under extreme environments. This trade-off leaves robustness and diversity difficult to achieve simultaneously. To mitigate these issues, we propose **C3-OWD**, a curriculum cross-modal contrastive learning framework that unifies both strengths. Stage 1 enhances robustness by pretraining with RGBT data, while Stage 2 improves generalization via vision-language alignment. To prevent catastrophic forgetting between two stages, we introduce an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) mechanism that theoretically guarantees preservation of pre-stage performance with bounded parameter lag and function consistency. Experiments on FLIR, OV-COCO, and OV-LVIS demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach: C3-OWD achieves 80.1 $AP^{50}$ on FLIR, 48.6 $AP^{50}_{Novel}$ on OV-COCO, and 35.7 $mAP_r$ on OV-LVIS, establishing competitive performance across both robustness and diversity evaluations. ![framework](./assets/framework_2_01.png) ## TODO List - [x] Upload our paper to arXiv and build project pages. - [x] Upload the code. - [ ] Release C3-OWD model. # 🤗 Prerequisite details ## Environment ```bash conda create -n C3-OWD python=3.8.10 -y pip install torch==1.13.0 torchvision==0.14.0 torchaudio==0.13.0 pip install -r requir

title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. While multistatic ISAC can increase sensing coverage with spatially distributed receivers, dense and dynamic clutter can significantly degrade bistatic range and Doppler estimation, leading to errors in target localization and velocity estimation. This paper presents a multistatic ISAC framework with clutter suppression for high-fidelity estimation of target position and velocity. Distributed clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers with varying Doppler spreads and radar cross sections to capture dense and dynamic clutter effects. A broad range of conventional signal processing baselines are evaluated for clutter suppression, showing limited robustness under strong clutter conditions. To address this limitation, deep learning-based clutter suppression methods are introduced to improve robustness against dense and dynamic clutter by employing residual and attention-enhanced deep neural network architectures that directly enhance target responses from clutter-contaminated observations. These methods substantially outperform conventional approaches in target position and velocity estimation across diverse clutter conditions in multistatic ISAC.

title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
summary: How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-\textsf{Majority}, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-\textsf{Majority} achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results. For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-\textsf{Majority} that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration. When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds. We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.

title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
summary: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.

title: AI in the EGI e-infrastructure -- Past experiences and future strategies
summary: The EGI Federation has provided federated e-infrastructure services to European and global science for over 15 years. We review EGI's early experiences with AI in the interTwin and iMagine Horizon Europe projects, which built digital twins in physics and environmental sciences and an image-analysis platform for aquatic research. We then examine how the AI landscape has changed since 2023 and argue that the focus of AI in science has shifted from model training to adapting and applying AI to specific domains, projects and questions. Building on these lessons, we present the AI strategy emerging from the EGI Federation Strategy 2026-2030, organised around three enablers: (1) an AI-ready infrastructure connecting compute, data and application resources across the continuum; (2) human skills to know what is possible with AI and how to implement it; and (3) trust, to run AI with confidence even in high-risk environments. We describe the projects implementing each enabler, including federated LLM inference, AI-ready data platforms and AI competence centres, and discuss a division of labour with EuroHPC's AI Factories, RAISE, research infrastructures and EOSC, in which EGI specialises in the customisation and long-term operation of AI for research.

title: SPECTRUM: A Strategic Framework and Technical Blueprint for European Exascale Research Data and Compute Infrastructure
summary: The HiLumi LHC, the SKA Observatory and LOFAR 2.0 will take High Energy Physics (HEP) and Radio Astronomy (RA) towards exabyte-scale data within the next decade, beyond the capacity of today's infrastructure. The SPECTRUM project responded with two documents built on the same evidence. A Technical Blueprint describes a European compute and data continuum as a capability map, consolidates the gaps found in HEP, RA and related use cases, and recommends technical actions in eight areas. A Strategic Research, Innovation and Deployment Agenda (SRIDA) organises thirteen priorities in four pillars, maps them to investment areas and European funding instruments, and phases them over a roadmap set against the timelines of the three instruments. This paper, by editors and contributors of both documents, summarises them, their consultative method and the impact the SRIDA expects.

title: Can We Rely on Language Models to Orchestrate Services across the Edge-Cloud Continuum?
summary: Service orchestration across the edge--cloud continuum increasingly uses language models (LMs) to translate intents and operational evidence into scheduling, configuration, diagnosis, and remediation decisions. Yet, useful model outputs do not by themselves establish dependable orchestration: reliability also depends on where the LM enters the decision process, what authority it is granted, how actions are constrained, and what system-level evidence supports the claimed effect. Existing surveys provide limited synthesis of the links between continuum-specific orchestration decisions, LM responsibility, operational authority, assurance controls, and supporting empirical evidence. We systematically review 39 primary studies and develop a five-dimensional analytical framework for connecting system context, orchestration decisions, LM agency, operational safeguards, and evaluation evidence. The synthesis reveals predominantly hybrid designs in which LMs support interpretation, candidate generation, and mitigation planning, while downstream components commonly retain feasibility enforcement and execution authority. Bounded closed-loop remediation is emerging, but continuum-specific constraints remain unevenly represented in decision formulations, and production-scale evidence across heterogeneous edge--cloud environments remains limited. These findings suggest that reliance on LM-enabled orchestration depends on aligning decision constraints, operational authority, safeguards, and evaluation evidence with the claimed system effect.

title: True 3D Holography: A Communication Service of Tomorrow and Its Requirements for a New Converged Cloud and Network Architecture on the Path to 6G
summary: Research project 6G NeXt is considering true 3D holography as a use case, setting requirements on the communication as well as the computing infrastructure. In a future holographic communication service, clients are widely spread in the network and cooperatively interact with each other. Especially for holographic communication high processing power is required as well. This makes a high-speed distributed backbone computing infrastructure, which realizes the concept of split computing, inevitable. Furthermore, tight integration between processing facilities and wireless networks is required in order to provide an immersive user experience. This paper illustrates true 3D holographic communication and its requirements. Afterward, an appropriate solution approach is elaborated. Here, novel technological approaches are discussed based on a proposed overall communication and computing architecture.

title: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for Modern LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading
summary: Modern LLMs strain device memory through large model weights and attention states, particularly in resource-constrained scenarios. Existing systems separately provision memory for model weights and attention states, imposing fixed fixed boundaries that cannot adapt to the changing memory demands of workloads. Under heavy workloads, insufficient state capacity limits request concurrency and reduces throughput; under light workloads, idle memory in one region cannot be reallocated to another, wasting device memory. Meanwhile, modern LLM architectures introduce heterogeneous tensors with diverse layouts and lifetimes, further complicating memory management. These problems motivate unified memory management for heterogeneous tensors. However, a shared pool alone does not make memory directly reusable across tensors with different allocation granularities and execution layouts. This paper presents Rimuru, a modern LLM serving system that unifies memory management through elastic expert offloading. Rimuru establishes a shared page pool to enables elastic memory sharing across heterogeneous tensors. To accommodate different allocation granularities, Rimuru introduces memory views that allow each tensor type to interpret the shared memory space using its own page size and page table. Furthermore, Rimuru combines huge-page alignment with a multi-level page allocator that splits and merges pages, enabling cross-type capacity reuse. A page-table-aware fused MoE kernel directly accesses non-contiguous expert weights, avoiding copy overhead. Building on these mechanisms, Rimuru employs a workload-aware adjuster that dynamically reallocates pages across tensor types according to runtime demands. Implemented on top of vLLM, Rimuru remains compatible with modern LLMs. Evaluations show that Rimuru achieves up to 19.03x baseline throughput and reduces TTFT by 98.1% on average.

title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets
summary: Large language model serving is limited by facility power. Energy per token determines how many tokens a datacenter can serve, while a latency target bounds how quickly each user receives them. During decode, every weight is read from memory for every generated token. Batching amortizes this read across users but makes no individual user faster. Speculative decoding does: a drafter proposes several future tokens, and the target model verifies them in a single forward pass that reuses the same weight read. Because every drafted token must be verified whether or not it is accepted, the energy speculation saves depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted. This saving is hard to pin down. It varies across target models from different attention families and across drafting schemes, and it depends on the text being served. Every drafter we evaluate accepts fewer tokens on conversation than on code, and every trained drafter accepts fewer on Romansh, a low-resource language, than on English. We measure speculative decoding under production serving conditions (SGLang, CUDA graphs enabled) on H100 and H200 GPUs, at batch sizes up to 64 across 5 corpora. On dense models, verification, not drafting, dominates the energy cost. The saving shrinks as the batch grows, because batching has already shared the weight read that speculation would divide among the accepted tokens. At large batch sizes, block drafters push verification past the balance point between arithmetic and memory traffic into the compute-bound regime, where the saving becomes a loss, and a drafter with low acceptance raises energy per token. Meeting a tighter latency target with speculation then costs additional energy. Larger batches lower energy per token without speculation. Speculation adds to that saving only when acceptance is high, and on the model we tested it leaves little headroom for latency-preserving DVFS.

title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
summary: As network scale and uncertainty complicate automated penetration testing, reinforcement learning (RL) environments must support controlled evaluation under defensive and non-stationary conditions. We present DYNAS (Dynamic Network Attack Simulator), which combines parameterized large-scale scenario generation with stateful intrusion detection responses, explicit scan false-positive and false-negative noise, temporary service unavailability, and duration-based action timeouts. We further introduce Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager--worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context. We compare Pen-DHRL with GNN, Invariant, and Attention baselines across four scenario variants and multiple training regimes. Under IDS-disabled training followed by IDS-enabled evaluation, Pen-DHRL obtains approximately 64\% and 24\% higher reward per step on Bridge and Dynamic, respectively, and approximately 26\% and 30\% more captured hosts on VarA and VarB than the next-best baseline. With all defensive dynamics active from the beginning of training, Pen-DHRL achieves positive mean episode returns in all four scenarios, whereas the flat baselines produce negative mean returns in all 12 architecture--scenario combinations; staged curriculum training produces positive mean returns across all 16 evaluated combinations.

title: Integer-Quantized Hierarchical Matrices with Adaptive Bit Allocation
summary: We present an adaptive bitwidth allocation method for quantizing low-rank factors in hierarchical matrices in order to decrease storage while meeting a given constraint on their reconstruction error. For the bitwidth allocation we formulate a discrete storage minimization problem and show that an optimal assignment can give larger singular values at least as many bits as smaller ones. We further develop a greedy algorithm that meets the specified max-norm quantization error budget. We investigate a hierarchical block partition in which all of the non-diagonal blocks are represented by quantized low-rank factors and only dense blocks remain dense; in this way a global reconstruction bound related to $η_k$ and $R_k$ is obtained, with the former and latter being bounds on the truncation and reconstruction arithmetic errors, respectively. Extensive simulations, carried out with kernel and BEM matrices under block-relative budgets, indicate that the proposed method achieves a reduction in storage of up to $44.3\times$ when compared to storing the complete matrix densely in FP64, and a reduction of up to $5.70\times$ when compared to the FP64 low-rank factors within the same partition, together with measured reconstruction errors that remained below the maximum norm bounds in all the hierarchical tests.

title: How Far Are We From On-Device VLM Inference? A Measurement Study on Edge NPUs
summary: Diverse optimizations spanning model architecture, inference runtime, and hardware acceleration have been proposed for on-device vision-language model (VLM) deployment on edge NPUs. Still, cross-layer coordination of VLM execution on edge NPUs remains largely underexplored. This paper presents an empirical measurement study across six representative VLMs, three real-world edge platforms, and ten multimodal benchmarks. Our evaluation drills down from end-to-end application-level latency and thermal traces down to low-level kernel-scale execution behaviors, challenging several widely held community assumptions. First, softmax dominates attention costs; even lookup-table-based softmax optimizations cannot eliminate pipeline bubbles that severely underutilize NPU matrix units. Second, theoretical speedups from linear attention vanish under real-NPU execution due to prohibitive tensor-rearrangement overhead. Third, no hardware backend universally dominates autoregressive decoding: attention-tensor-shaped parallelism dictates NPU efficiency and shifts the CPU-NPU performance balance. We further find task-specific Sweet Resolutions for VLMs, which deliver meaningful accuracy gains at only modest latency overhead. Complementing these findings, we provide actionable cross-layer recommendations for hardware architects, runtime developers, and model designers.

title: NORmal: Architecting 3D Ferroelectric NOR Flash as Main Memory -- From Co-Fabricated BEOL Arrays to 200B-Class Multi-Agent LLMs in a Smartphone
summary: Smartphone agents increasingly work as teams, in which a large planner directs parallel workers across long sessions. Running such a team on the device requires 200B-class models and contexts that exceed phone DRAM many times over, yet existing tiers treat flash as storage: UFS starves per-token weight streaming, and mobile High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) needs a redesigned SoC and cannot absorb continuous KV writes. We show that a non-volatile memory can join an unmodified LPDDR6 bus as a plain rank only if its access latency fits the DRAM timing window, a condition no NAND tier meets. We present NORmal, to our knowledge the first main-memory architecture for 3D ferroelectric NOR flash. We have fabricated and experimentally characterized back-end-of-line (BEOL) 3D FeNOR arrays that co-integrate dense 3-bit MLC and fast, high-endurance in-place-writable SLC with sub-7.5 ns sensing. NORmal turns these co-fabricated arrays into a byte-addressable, deterministic-timing load/store rank on an unmodified LPDDR6 interface through an under-array DRAM-emulation bridge, staggered bank reads with zero-cycle weight swizzling, and posted SLC writes. Across this rank and DRAM, NORmal places agent state by mutability and lifetime rather than by hotness, serving 200B-class models and persistent planner contexts in place while dynamically partitioning subchannels across agent phases. In serving-level simulation on production agent traces, NORmal is 8.9$\times$--28.0$\times$ faster than UFS offloading, within 0.4% of an unlimited-DRAM ideal, and 2.8$\times$--6.3$\times$ faster than HBF on sessions beyond 256K tokens, with 8.1$\times$--17.8$\times$ less memory energy per token.

title: PhOSv1: Efficient Scaling of Model Sleeping on a Single Server for Autoscaling with GPU-Context Deduplication
summary: Autoscaling is a key mechanism in model-as-a-service systems, where fast scale-up is essential because the scale-up time directly determines how long a model service remains overloaded, which in turn governs serving quality. The state-of-the-art approach, model sleeping, adopted by mainstream serving engines including vLLM and SGLang, achieves near-zero-cost scale-up by pausing pre-spawned engines on the GPU. However, sleeping is not a free lunch: each sleeping model must keep its GPU context resident, and this cost grows linearly with the number of models, degrading serving performance. Because providers must support many models, they face a dilemma between fast scale-up for all models and high service performance. In this paper, we show that a single server can keep many models asleep without paying this GPU context tax. The key observation is that the contexts of sleeping models are largely duplicated: the driver (CUDA) context can be shared across models, and their GPU kernel binaries overlap heavily due to common operators and libraries. PhOSv1 deduplicates this context by transparently delegating each engine's GPU context allocation to a central daemon through API remoting; therefore, a single server can keep far more models asleep than current engines allow. Our evaluation shows that PhOSv1 matches the scale-up time of vanilla vLLM sleep mode while substantially reducing the GPU memory footprint, improving end-to-end multi-model serving performance.

title: An Exact Parallel Dense Gauss-Seidel Algorithm with Trade-Offs between Parallel Execution Time and Preprocessing Time
summary: The Gauss-Seidel iterative method is commonly used for solving systems of linear equations because of its good convergence properties. However, the Gauss-Seidel algorithm cannot be easily parallelized because of the data dependencies existing at each iteration. The best parallel execution time for dense systems of equations is $O(n)$ given that enough processors are available and no preprocessing is performed. In this paper we propose a new parallel Gauss-Seidel algorithm which is capable of achieving better parallel runtimes at the expense of more preprocessing time. The algorithm can be tuned in order to provide convenient trade-offs between the preprocessing time and the best parallel runtime achievable by the algorithm.

title: FedMaJ: Ordinal Meta-Aggregation for Federated Learning Using Majority-Judgment Voting
summary: Federated learning traditionally relies on a fixed aggregation rule despite shifting client state and wireless dynamics. We present FedMaJ, a framework that dynamically selects aggregation rules via Majority Judgment voting. During voting rounds, clients evaluate candidate models across performance, resource utilization, channel condition, and fairness metrics. The server adopts the majority-preferred rule and retains it until the next vote, scheduled dynamically based on accuracy trends. Evaluated in over-the-air federated learning with explicit energy and resource cost modeling, synthetic and Fashion-MNIST experiments show that FedMaJ achieves competitive learning performance and superior aggregation-influence fairness. Under extreme-evaluation perturbations, Majority Judgment yields significantly more stable rule selections than mean-based scoring, establishing ordinal voting as a robust control layer for adaptive aggregation.

title: TRACEs: Fine-Grained Embedded Provenance for Distributed Scientific Workflows
summary: Large-scale scientific workflows run on distributed HPC resources, making it hard to explain how scientific data products are generated and why similar workflow executions can yield very different results. Existing systems usually focus on either distributed workflow execution or provenance management and rarely treat fine-grained provenance as an intrinsic property of distributed scientific data artifacts. We present TRACEs (Traceable Runtime for Advanced Containerized Executions), a provenance architecture for distributed containerized scientific workflows that embeds data lineage and execution context directly in every generated data artifact. By decoupling provenance from workflow orchestration, TRACEs generalizes artifact-centric provenance from local container runs to distributed workflows while remaining compatible with existing workflow management systems. We evaluate TRACEs on a seven-stage E. coli variant-calling workflow distributed across multiple HPC nodes. Our results show 100% provenance completeness under distributed execution, about 59% less intermediate storage via sparse IMG containers, and runtime and zero-copy I/O throughput comparable to fixed-size SIF containers, plus provenance-guided explanations of workflow variability that trace a 200-fold difference in variant counts to differences in input sequencing data without re-executing the workflow.

title: LAMP: LLM-Driven Analog Placement through Adaptive Tool Composition
summary: Analog placement requires circuit-specific trade-offs among area, matching, routability, and electrical performance. Balancing these trade-offs through predefined objectives and fixed placement flows remains difficult. In this paper, we propose an analog placement framework in which a large language model (LLM) acts as a layout engineer through composable placement components. These components support constraint management, placement and legalization, and lightweight evaluation of routability and electrical performance. Using multimodal checkpoints of the initial and evolving design, the LLM selects and combines components to construct and revise its own placement flow. It also adapts the placement hierarchy by reopening modules or partitioning and regrouping devices, allowing local layouts to respond to global design needs. An experience skill provides reusable design knowledge to guide these decisions. Evaluation on two SMIC 180 nm circuits shows that the framework reduces placement area and improves most measured post-layout performance metrics.

title: Enabling Dynamic Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuit Simulations
summary: Studies of quantum algorithms often simulate se- quences of circuits whose number of qubits changes from one circuit to the next, such as instances of increasing size of the same problem. Since each additional qubit doubles the state- vector, every circuit needs a different number of nodes, which a fixed allocation on a shared High-Performance Computing (HPC) system cannot provide: a job sized for the largest circuit leaves most of its nodes idle, and one job per circuit adds scheduler interactions and queue waits. We make the QuEST state-vector simulator malleable with the Dynamic Management of Resources (DMR) framework, so that a single job resizes between circuits. Because no state-vector exists between circuits, reconfigurations require no data redistribution and no changes to the simulation kernels, and a checkpoint holding the index of the next circuit is enough to resume. A right-sizing policy derives the number of nodes from the number of qubits, and the circuit_executor API hides reconfigurations from the user. We evaluate the reconfiguration overhead on MareNostrum 5 and show that a single job can run a batch of circuits of different sizes, adapting its allocation to each of them with negligible overhead.

title: Caerus: Prefetching by Thinking Globally and Acting Locally
summary: Modern processors rely heavily on data prefetching to bridge the growing performance gap between computation and memory accesses. In offset prefetching, prefetches are issued at an address delta relative to the most recently observed access, selecting deltas that have exhibited high coverage in the recent access-stream history. The Best-Offset Prefetcher (BOP) exemplifies this approach by selecting a single uniformly-issued global offset that delivers timely prefetches. However, its lack of context-sensitive accuracy tracking results in significantly increased DRAM traffic and sometimes disappointing performance. Conversely, Berti, the state-of-the-art offset prefetcher, achieves impressive prefetching performance and accuracy. However, its Program-Counter (PC)-local approach to extracting offsets limits its ability to capture global memory patterns, meaning there are many scenarios where simpler global offset prefetchers, such as BOP, outperform it. Observing the limitations of contemporary offset prefetchers, we present Caerus: an offset prefetcher that employs PC-local filtering on multiple non-overlapping globally derived offsets. Caerus extracts multiple offsets from the global memory trace and maximizes their combined coverage by training each offset only on accesses not already covered by previously learned offsets. The accuracy of each extracted offset is tracked per-PC based on whether it can cover future accesses for any PC. This allows Caerus to address complex delta patterns while maintaining high accuracy. In SPECspeed 2017, Caerus gains a geomean speedup of 8.3%, outperforming Berti by 2.0% while achieving low hardware and DRAM-traffic overhead.

title: Device-Induced Mobility Heterogeneity and Its Impact on Federated Next-Location Prediction
summary: Predicting human mobility is central to network management, urban planning, and location-based services, yet privacy concerns are increasingly pushing such tasks toward federated learning. A key challenge in this setting is the strong heterogeneity of mobility data across users, which leads to non-IID data distributions and can significantly impact model performance and fairness. In this paper, we present a large-scale measurement study of device-level mobility heterogeneity using data from a major MNO in a dense European capital. Our dataset comprises mobility traces derived from network events, covering over 50,000 UEs across 178 smartphone models. We group devices into tiers based on their market segment and show that mobility characteristics, such as spatial range and regularity, vary systematically across these tiers, revealing a previously underexplored source of bias in mobility data. We investigate the implications of this heterogeneity on the use case of federated next-location prediction. In particular, we find that balancing device tiers across silos through tier-aware client selection yields the best results, improving fairness by up to 34.49% without degrading accuracy. In contrast, a FedProx-only approach achieves a 21.46% fairness improvement, offering a reasonable alternative when device information is unavailable, though with lower overall gains.

title: Sandman: Building and Operating Sandboxes for Agentic Reinforcement Learning on Shared Kubernetes
summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) often requires repeated tool calls in task-specific environments. A training job may create thousands of these environments in bursts while sharing a cluster with other jobs. We present Sandman, a sandbox service built and operated at Amazon for agent tool execution and evaluation. It serves multiple production agentic RL workloads on shared Kubernetes. A training framework supplies a task image and uses commands and file operations in the returned sandbox. Files and processes persist across calls until the framework releases the environment. Sandman manages creation, readiness and cleanup. Each sandbox is a Kubernetes pod with a small daemon mounted into the unmodified image. In a scale test, Sandman held 11,858 concurrent tiny sandboxes. Four production SWE-bench Verified training campaigns created 3.1 million sandboxes in October 2026. We report the design trade-offs and operational lessons from handling creation bursts, preparing task environments, reclaiming abandoned sandboxes, and running evaluation under controlled conditions. We will open-source Sandman's daemon, provider and pool.

title: Federated Agentic AI for Interference-Aware Adaptive Spectrum Coordination
summary: Emerging intelligent wireless networks increasingly rely on autonomous AI agents to adapt spectrum usage to dynamic and heterogeneous operating conditions. However, collective learning is challenging when agents experience different local interference environments and cannot exchange raw observations due to communication-overhead and privacy constraints. We propose Federated Agentic Spectrum Coordination with Interference Awareness (FASCIA), a federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for adaptive spectrum coordination. In FASCIA, each network manager acts as an autonomous AI agent that perceives its local interference environment, accumulates experience in a persistent local memory, and learns an adaptive spectrum coordination policy through local interactions. Coordination among agents is achieved through periodic federated aggregation of locally trained models, without exchanging raw sensing data or experience. Since spectrum decisions made by one agent alter the environments observed by others, local learning is inherently heterogeneous and coupled. FASCIA employs proximal regularization to mitigate the resulting model drift and explicitly accounts for inter-carrier interference arising from partially overlapping channels. FASCIA is the first federated agentic AI framework to address this challenging interference-coupled spectrum coordination setting. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FASCIA achieves performance close to the centralized benchmark while avoiding raw-experience exchange and maintaining effectiveness across heterogeneous network configurations.

title: MRUD: Maximally Redundant Unsigned Digit Number Systems for High-Performance Arithmetic Units
summary: Signed digit redundant number systems such as Maximally Redundant Signed Digit (MRSD) enable carry-free addition but introduce significant overhead in multiplication due to the presence of both positive and negative bits. While Unsigned Digit Redundant (UDR) systems have shown promise in radix-2, their extension to higher radices remains unexplored. This work presents the first generalized Maximally Redundant Unsigned Digit (MRUD) number systems for high-radix arithmetic, extending UDR representations from radix-2 to radix-$2^h$ while preserving carry-free addition. The proposed framework includes digit encoding, digit extension, arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, and multiplication), sign inversion, forward/reverse conversion algorithms, overflow/underflow detection, and hardware architectures for both signed and unsigned MRUD representations. Unlike MRSD, which is inherently limited to signed arithmetic, MRUD supports both signed and unsigned representations, similar to conventional binary systems. Evaluations across three multiplier modes---RRR (Redundant inputs, Redundant output), BBR (Binary inputs, Redundant output), and BBB (Binary inputs, Binary output)---as well as Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units, using the FreePDK 45nm library, demonstrate that MRUD achieves up to 30\% lower delay, 26\% smaller area, and 87\% lower power than MRSD. In BBR mode, MRUD achieves up to 43\% delay reduction over the best conventional architecture for 32$\times$32 operands, while in Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units, performing reverse conversion only once at the end yields up to 64\% higher throughput than DesignWare and over 150\% higher than Wallace. These results demonstrate that MRUD enables high-radix redundant arithmetic with significantly improved multiplier and MAC performance, making it an efficient alternative to conventional signed digit redundant number systems.

title: Improving Energy Efficiency of Uplink RSMA via Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
summary: This paper investigates an uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network empowered by a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) to maximize energy efficiency (EE). To overcome the amplitude-only measurement limitation of the considered direct readout RAQR, we devise a phase alignment mechanism that linearizes the received signal while retaining full channel energy, thereby enabling tractable optimization. The resulting non-convex fractional EE problem is transformed via Dinkelbach's method. For IoT scenarios with symmetric rate requirements, we derive exact closed-form power allocation from the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, which yields a globally optimal bisection search with negligible computational latency. For asymmetric rate requirements, we develop a generalized block coordinate descent-based power allocation (BCD-PA) framework that eliminates reliance on expensive interior-point solvers. We further propose a low-complexity paired allocation (LC-Paired) that exploits user pairing and closed-form bandwidth solutions via the Lambert-W function. Simulation results confirm that the KKT-based scheme attains the highest EE, while the BCD-PA offers a flexible complexity-performance trade-off. The LC-Paired scheme drastically reduces computational cost with only moderate EE degradation.

title: RV2GC: Reconstructing the Garbling Boundary in a RISC-V Garbled Processor
summary: Programmable garbled-circuit execution must balance the benefits of cross-program reuse against the cost of repeated work during secure execution. A complete garbled processor provides a fixed circuit for many programs, but its evaluator repeatedly visits processor-wide structures even when only a small part performs the current protected computation. We present RV2GC, which reconstructs the garbling boundary around a fixed library of RISC-V instruction circuits. Public scheduling and operand routing operate outside the circuit topologies; persistent label-encoded state connects independently invoked garbled instruction circuits and instruction-specific garbling-free paths through a common interface. A Conditional-execution Stack and protected commits support secret-dependent branches, bounded loops, and secret-indexed memory access under public scheduling, keeping instruction and memory-address sequences independent of private inputs. Across nine benchmarks, measured ARM2GC-to-RV2GC runtime ratios range from 12.81 to 4,043. In terms of circuit size, the largest listed instruction circuit has 3,386 gates, corresponding to 2.044% and 0.393% of the 256-byte and 4,096-byte Amber processors, respectively. Additional comparisons quantify schedule storage, communication, and the cost of secret-dependent execution.

title: LLM Agent-Based Design of RISC-V CPUs with FPGA-in-the-Loop Evaluation
summary: Long-run RTL simulation of CPU candidates can take hours, while short diagnostic runs may miss performance degradation that emerges later in execution. This evaluation cost can delay design decisions in LLM-agent-based CPU development. We present a development environment in which LLM agents implement CPU candidates on an FPGA and use on-board performance measurements to guide design decisions. We applied it to the human-supervised development of a single-cycle RV32I core into a three-wide out-of-order RV32IM core. The final design reaches 5.61 CoreMark/MHz at 130 MHz on a Artix-7 FPGA. For the same CPU candidate running 8,000 CoreMark iterations, FPGA evaluation, including implementation, was 9.6x faster than single-threaded RTL simulation. In one case, board measurements revealed long-run performance degradation in a candidate that improved in a short diagnostic run. The result guided candidate selection and led to RTL-based root-cause analysis and a fix.

title: Quantifying the Relay-Coverage Trade-off in Mobile Multihop Flooding
summary: Network-wide flooding in mobile multihop networks selects relays from locally maintained topology information. Mobility makes this information outdated, leaving two basic responses: add redundant relays or refresh the topology and re-select relays more frequently. How these mechanisms trade reliability for overhead, however, is not well quantified. We quantify this trade-off on a public trace of 157 vehicles using Optimized Link State Routing version 2 (OLSRv2) and exact minimum-cost relay sets. Twofold coverage increases median relay-cover lifetime by only 2.3x, rather than about an order of magnitude as predicted by an independent-hazard model. The limitation is structural: 43.6 % of two-hop neighbours have only one possible relay, and newly appearing neighbours invalidate existing covers. Moreover, the delivery gain of a second relay falls from 0.061 to 0.016 when relay selection uses instantaneous link state, showing that redundancy mainly compensates for outdated topology information. Relay coverage and topology refresh therefore form a measurable redundancy-freshness trade-off rather than independent robustness mechanisms. In our trace, twofold coverage has lower overhead below about 100 bit/s of application flooding per node, whereas fresher topology information has lower overhead above it. This makes relay redundancy a load-dependent design choice rather than a fixed heuristic robustness setting.

title: APPlace: Co-Optimizing Device Locations and Access Points for Routing-Aware Analog Placement
summary: Analog layout automation remains challenging in Analog/Mixed-Signal circuit design, because parasitics and mismatches introduced during layout strongly affect circuit performance. Placement is especially critical among the layout stages, as it constrains the routing solution space and the achievable post-layout performance. Existing analytical placement methods optimize device coordinates under center-based wirelength proxies and leave access point (AP) selection to routing. In analog circuits, however, a routing pin is an extended piece of terminal metal rather than a fixed point, and the best AP on it depends on where the other connected devices are placed, so a coordinate-only placement optimizes for connection points that the router will not use. We present APPlace, a routing-aware analog placement framework that co-optimizes device locations and AP selections during global placement, followed by a legalization stage that preserves the structure established by global placement. Experimental results on four real-world analog benchmarks show that APPlace achieves better overall post-layout performance than representative baselines at comparable layout area. Ablation studies further show that removing AP co-optimization causes up to a 13 dB CMRR loss among the OTA benchmarks and a 23% increase in comparator delay.

title: SeQUeNCe.DQC: Full-stack Simulation of Distributed Quantum Computing
summary: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) connects multiple quantum processing units to overcome the scale limits of monolithic hardware. We introduce SeQUeNCe.DQC, a new top-level module within the SeQUeNCe package that compiles monolithic circuits into topology-aware execution plans and coordinates their execution using SeQUeNCe's existing quantum-network modules and protocols. We validate SeQUeNCe.DQC by reproducing a two-node trapped-ion Grover experiment in simulation and comparing success probabilities with the reported 71% benchmark. We then evaluate how compiler strategy, topology, and memory capacity jointly govern distributed circuit execution time and success rate. In these experiments, our hybrid compilers successfully identified mixed TeleGate/TeleData execution plans that outperformed pure gate-teleportation strategies. By capturing the physical overhead of distributed quantum primitives, SeQUeNCe.DQC provides a rigorous platform for co-designing DQC software and hardware architectures.

title: CoraLive: Ultra-Low-Power Underwater Vision for Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring
summary: Effective coral reef protection and restoration demands continuous, long-term underwater monitoring. However, current solutions largely rely on fragmented, manual labor and costly infrastructure, or are severely limited by constrained battery lifespans. In this paper, we present CoraLive, an ultra-low-power underwater camera system for long-term, continuous coral reef monitoring. CoraLive presents a decoupled underwater-shore co-design that minimizes on-board computation and storage, offloading heavy reconstruction and segmentation tasks to offline shore-side processing. To achieve this, CoraLive introduces a dual-rate sensing scheme combining frequent low-resolution frames with sparse high-fidelity samples and a content-adaptive update mechanism that extracts and stores only compact, task-specific data, eliminating the need to save raw video frames. We implement CoraLive on a custom STM32U575-based dual-camera prototype with device-level computation and storage optimization. Compared with raw recording, CoraLive reduces daily storage by $4.51\times$ and average power by $7.78\times$, extending battery lifetime from 20.4 to 159.5~days while retaining high-accuracy segmentation and reconstruction. Further validated in a real-world underwater deployment, we envision CoraLive as a pioneering step for ubiquitous long-term coral reef underwater monitoring.

title: Energy-Efficient Memristor Accelerator for Depression Detection with a CNN-LSTM Hybrid Model
summary: Early screening of depression requires efficient analysis of audio and speech data, while conventional CPU and GPU platforms incur high latency and energy consumption for CNN-LSTM inference. To address this challenge, we propose a unified resistive RAM (ReRAM) processing-in-memory accelerator for a CNN-LSTM attention workload. The architecture integrates convolutional, recurrent, attention, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) stages within a crossbar-based framework, reducing intermediate data movement between spatial and temporal branches. CNN operations are mapped through im2col-based vectorization, while LSTM gate computations are reformulated using concatenated input-state vectors and mapped onto ReRAM crossbars. We further provide module-level workload breakdown, parameter sensitivity analysis, and matched-workload context against representative ReRAM/PIM accelerators. Experimental results show 32.1 times and 9.3 times latency reduction over CPU and GPU baselines, respectively, with about 160 times and 140 times energy reduction. Simplified weight-perturbation tests characterize ASLF sensitivity in an untrained pipeline with synthetic spectrogram-shaped inputs. Task-level prediction accuracy and robustness remain to be evaluated.

title: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases
summary: Training language models whose parameters and optimizer state exceed a single node's memory requires sharding these tensors across devices. Under tensor parallelism (TP) or fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP), matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon introduce communication to perform global matrix operations across shards. We propose Dobb (Distributed Optimizer with Block-diagonal Eigenbases), a matrix-aware optimizer designed to compute updates locally within parameter shards. Dobb approximates the input-activation second moment with diagonal blocks and tracks a complete basis within each block. It projects momentum into these bases, applies sign normalization to the coefficients, and reconstructs the update. When each block lies within one shard under TP or FSDP, Dobb applies its matrix update locally, requiring no communication beyond data-parallel synchronization of the activation second moments. We benchmark Dobb against Dion, a distributed matrix-aware optimizer designed to retain the benefits of orthonormalized updates while reducing communication. On GPT-2 XL (1.56B parameters), Dobb with 16 blocks reaches a validation loss of 2.476, compared with 2.511 for Dion at rank fraction 1/16. Under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs, Dobb reduces the amortized optimizer-call time from 124.1 ms for Dion to 9.2 ms.

title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
summary: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. In SKY130, the agent designed a shared constant-gm bias and six opamps (5T, folded-cascode and telescopic OTAs; Miller, folded-cascode and telescopic two-stage) for fun >= 50 MHz, PM >= 60 degrees, SR 25 V/μs into 1 pF and a minimum dc gain of 30 to 60 dB. All six layouts are DRC-clean and LVS-matched, and their extracted netlists meet every target at all 15 PVT corners ( fun >= 53.7 MHz, PM >= 62.1 degrees, SR >= 27.9 V/μs). The benchmark netlists are released at https://github.com/AMPICLab/AMPICBench.

title: Learning to Formulate: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Design of AI Infrastructure through Progressive Optimization and Verification
summary: AI infrastructure, the chips and software that train and serve AI models, is designed in layers. Layers make the system manageable, but they also fix which choices an optimizer can consider. Gains that need the chip and its software to change together are excluded before optimization begins: the formulation leaves them out. Language-model agents make it possible to revisit these boundaries, but an agent's proposal cannot show by itself that a design is correct or optimal. We present Formulaic, a flow that divides the work. The agent writes the formulation, a mathematical solver optimizes within it, and verification and measurement check its assumptions and results. The agent refines the problem step by step, from the computation graph toward the chip. Each step is a template: a family of programs with the conditions under which they are correct. Wall relaxation searches the chip by pricing the hardware limits that bind the software. This paper takes a first step, through separate studies rather than one end-to-end run. On NVIDIA GB10, templates the agent wrote run complete Qwen3-8B layers $1.075\times$ faster than SGLang. In a simulated Ventus GPU study, joint design cuts the worst-scenario cycles of Qwen2.5-0.5B to 0.428 of the reference, against 0.934 for software alone. On a five-step GEMM refinement chain, reusing proofs makes checking $2.51\times$ faster.

title: More Is Better? Exploring Latent Correspondence in Federated Hypergraph Learning
summary: Federated hypergraph learning with latent cross-client hyperedge correspondence poses fundamental identifiability and computational challenges, as the same local release can correspond to multiple global hypergraph structures. We characterize the tractability of recovering these latent correspondences, showing tractable pairwise assignment but generally intractable multi-client hyperedge matching. Building on this characterization, we derive a cross-entropy decomposition that reveals when local prediction can outperform predictors fitted with additional cross-client information. Motivated by this principle, we introduce Federated Adaptive Spectral Training with Representation Alignment (FedASTRA), which learns correspondence-invariant diffusion representations through adaptive heat diffusion and masked latent prediction while communicating model parameters only. We establish its asymptotic optimality with respect to the permitted local information and prove global population-risk convergence under explicit conditions on recovery, representation, and update alignment. Experiments on eight real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of FedASTRA against identifier-free federated graph and hypergraph methods. On ogbn-papers100M, FedASTRA reaches the performance-communication Pareto frontier, achieving 50.07 Accuracy and 29.73 Macro-F1 while communicating only 59.60 MiB per round.

title: Energy-Efficient FPGA Implementation of an End-to-End Cosine-Domain CNN Using High-Level Synthesis
summary: The computational cost of conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) limits their deployment in low-power devices for high-speed edge AI applications. This paper presents an end-to-end cosine-domain CNN (CD-CNN) architecture for energy-efficient FPGA inference using high-level synthesis (HLS). The proposed architecture performs intermediate feature extraction using real-valued DCT-domain representations, avoiding complex-valued arithmetic and intermediate inverse transforms between spectral layers. The design is implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ XCKU5P FPGA and evaluated against a fully spectral Fourier-domain CNN (FD-CNN) under consistent network and implementation constraints. Experiments on the MNIST and 94-class ASCII datasets show that the CD-CNN reduces normalized resource utilization and improves inference throughput on both datasets. Its energy efficiency reaches 112.91 frames/J for MNIST and 101.27 frames/J for ASCII, corresponding to improvements of $1.51\times$ and $2.76\times$, respectively, over the fully spectral FD-CNN architecture. Furthermore, compared to the previous GPU-based fully spectral CD-CNN implementation, the proposed end-to-end FPGA implementation improves energy efficiency by $12.96\times$.
